description: Authenticated commerce core: per-user cart, saved addresses, order placement/checkout with MOCKED payment and gift-point redemption, order history with buy-again, and backend-enforced cancel-within-48h. All endpoints authenticate the JWT and scope strictly to the owner. Payment is fully mocked: no gateway, no payment-method selection; the order is created with status 'paid' on checkout (the frontend Pay button drives this), payment_method defaults to 'MOCK'. Depends on FEAT-002 (cart/address/order tables), FEAT-003 (auth guard), and FEAT-004 (book prices/stock). Satisfies journey items 2,8,9,10,11,12 on the backend.
steps: Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\cart.ts (all routes guarded, scoped to the user's cart row, created lazily if absent): GET /cart returns items joined to books with unit price (paise), line totals, subtotal, and item count. POST /cart/items (body: bookId, quantity) adds or increments, validating stock and that the book exists; returns the updated cart. PATCH /cart/items/:id (body: quantity) updates quantity (quantity 0 removes) only if the item belongs to the user's cart else 404. DELETE /cart/items/:id removes it (404 if not owned). Validate bodies with Elysia t; consistent JSON errors.

Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\addresses.ts (guarded, scoped to user_id): GET /addresses lists the user's addresses. POST /addresses creates one (label, recipient, line1, line2?, city, state, postal_code, country, is_default?) — if is_default, clear the flag on the user's other addresses. PATCH /addresses/:id updates an owned address (404 if not owned). DELETE /addresses/:id removes an owned address (404 if not owned).

Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\orders.ts (guarded). POST /orders (body: address_id, redeem_points?:integer>=0; payment_method optional defaulting to 'MOCK'): in a single DB transaction — load the user's cart (400 if empty); verify the address_id belongs to the user (404/400 otherwise); re-read book prices/stock from the DB (never trust client amounts) and verify stock, decrement stock; compute subtotal_cents; clamp redeem_points to the user's gift_points balance AND to the subtotal (1 point = a documented paise value, state it in findings), compute total_cents = subtotal - redemption; decrement the user's gift_points by points_redeemed; compute points_earned (e.g. floor(total paid / documented rupee-per-point)) and credit them; snapshot the chosen address as JSON; set status 'paid', payment_method 'MOCK', placed_at = now, cancellable_until = now + 48h; insert order + order_items (with title/author/unit_price snapshots); clear the cart; return the created order.

In src/api/orders.ts add GET /orders (list the user's orders, newest first, with items and a computed isCancellable = now < cancellable_until && status=='paid'), GET /orders/:id (owned only, else 404), POST /orders/:id/cancel (owned only; ENFORCE server-side: if status != 'paid' return 409; if now > cancellable_until return 403/409 { error: 'Cancellation window expired' } — compare against stored placed_at/cancellable_until, NEVER a client value; on success set status 'cancelled', restore each order_item's stock, and refund points_redeemed back to the user's gift_points while reversing points_earned), and POST /orders/:id/buy-again (owned only; re-add that order's books to the current cart respecting current stock; return the updated cart).

Mount cart + addresses + orders route modules in src/api/index.ts (.use). Document the points->currency conversion and welcome-points policy in this FEAT's findings so FEAT-006 displays them consistently.

Create c:\Users\PravallikaP\Documents\FDE capstone\online_bookstore\src\api\commerce.test.ts (temp seeded DB, two registered users A and B): A adds a cart item, adds an address, checks out (status 'paid', total reflects redemption, stock decremented, cart cleared, points earned); GET /orders shows the order with isCancellable true; buy-again re-adds items to A's cart; cancel within window succeeds (stock restored, points refunded); construct/insert an order row for A with placed_at older than 48h (and cancellable_until in the past) and assert POST /orders/:id/cancel is REJECTED server-side (403/409) and the order stays 'paid'; redeem_points exceeding balance is clamped (never negative total); and ISOLATION: user B gets 404/empty on A's cart items, addresses, orders, and cannot cancel/buy-again A's order.
acceptance_criteria: Cart, address, and order endpoints require a valid JWT and operate only on the authenticated user's data; a second user can never read or mutate the first user's cart/orders/addresses/points.

POST /api/orders creates a 'paid' order from the cart using server-recomputed prices, captures the chosen address snapshot, applies clamped gift-point redemption, decrements stock, credits earned points, and clears the cart.

POST /api/orders/:id/cancel succeeds within 48h (restoring stock and refunding redeemed points) and is rejected server-side when placed_at is older than 48h, based on stored timestamps not client input.
POST /api/orders/:id/buy-again re-adds the order's books to the current user's cart.
`bun test` passes commerce.test.ts (including the >48h rejection and cross-user isolation cases); `bunx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
verification: Run `bun test src/api/commerce.test.ts` (and full `bun test`) and confirm all pass, especially the >48h cancel rejection and the user-isolation assertions.
Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero errors.

Boot the server background/bounded and with Invoke-RestMethod using a user's $token: POST /api/cart/items, POST /api/addresses, POST /api/orders (address_id + redeem_points), GET /api/orders, POST /api/orders/:id/buy-again, POST /api/orders/:id/cancel (within window succeeds). Register a SECOND user and confirm GET /api/orders and /api/cart for them do not expose the first user's data. Stop the server afterward.
findings:
DONE. All acceptance criteria met. `bun test` 54/54 pass (21 in commerce.test.ts incl. the >48h cancel rejection and full cross-user isolation set); `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; live background-boot probe passed end-to-end (register A -> add cart item -> add address -> checkout 'paid'/'MOCK' -> order history -> buy-again -> cancel-within-window success) and the second-user isolation probe (B sees empty cart/orders, 404 on A's order, 401 unauthenticated). Server was stopped afterward; no process left running. Payment is FULLY MOCKED (no gateway, no method selection): checkout always creates status 'paid', payment_method defaults to 'MOCK'.

=== MONEY + POINTS CONVERSION (FEAT-006 MUST display these consistently) ===
All *_cents are INTEGER paise (₹1 = 100 paise); UI divides by 100 and formats with ₹. Constants exported from src/api/orders.ts:
  PAISE_PER_POINT = 100         -> REDEMPTION: 1 gift point = ₹1 = 100 paise off the subtotal.
  PAISE_PER_EARNED_POINT = 10000 -> EARNING: 1 point per ₹100 actually PAID, i.e. points_earned = floor(total_cents / 10000).
Redemption is clamped SERVER-SIDE to min(redeem_points, user.gift_points, floor(subtotal_cents / 100)); total_cents = subtotal_cents - points_redeemed*100 can never go negative. gift_points is adjusted on checkout as (-points_redeemed + points_earned) in one UPDATE. On cancel the reverse is applied (+points_redeemed - points_earned) and stock is restored per order_item.
WELCOME-POINTS POLICY: register (FEAT-003) seeds gift_points = 0. There is NO signup bonus; points accrue purely from purchases. The frontend should show the balance from /api/auth/me (or /api/auth/points) and refresh it after every order/cancel since both mutate the balance.

=== ENDPOINTS (all under /api, all JWT-guarded via authGuard, scoped to the authenticated user) ===
CART (src/api/cart.ts, prefix /cart):
  GET    /api/cart              -> CartView
  POST   /api/cart/items        body { bookId:int>=1, quantity:int>=1 } add/increment, validates stock+existence -> CartView (409 'Insufficient stock', 404 'Book not found')
  PATCH  /api/cart/items/:id    body { quantity:int>=0 } 0 removes; 404 if not owned; 409 over stock -> CartView
  DELETE /api/cart/items/:id    404 if not owned -> CartView
  CartView shape: { items: CartItemView[], subtotal_cents:number, item_count:number }
  CartItemView: { id, book_id, title, author, cover_url, unit_price_cents, quantity, line_total_cents, stock }  (id = cart_items.id; use it for PATCH/DELETE)
ADDRESSES (src/api/addresses.ts, prefix /addresses):
  GET    /api/addresses         -> { items: AddressRow[] }  (default first, then id ASC)
  POST   /api/addresses         body { label, recipient, line1, line2?, city, state, postal_code, country, is_default? } -> { address: AddressRow }  (setting is_default clears the flag on the user's other addresses)
  PATCH  /api/addresses/:id     partial body (same fields, all optional) -> { address: AddressRow }  (404 if not owned)
  DELETE /api/addresses/:id     -> { success:true }  (404 if not owned)
  AddressRow: { id, user_id, label, recipient, line1, line2, city, state, postal_code, country, is_default (0|1) }
ORDERS (src/api/orders.ts, prefix /orders):
  POST   /api/orders            body { address_id:int>=1, redeem_points?:int>=0, payment_method?:string } -> 201 { order: OrderView }. Checkout runs in ONE transaction: re-reads book prices/stock from the DB (NEVER trusts client amounts), verifies+decrements stock (409 'Insufficient stock for ...'), computes subtotal, clamps redemption, computes total+earned points, adjusts gift_points, snapshots the chosen address as JSON, inserts order (status 'paid', placed_at=now ISO, cancellable_until=now+48h ISO) + order_items (title/author/unit_price snapshots), clears the cart. 400 'Cart is empty', 404 'Address not found'.
  GET    /api/orders            -> { orders: OrderView[] } newest first (ORDER BY datetime(placed_at) DESC, id DESC)
  GET    /api/orders/:id        -> { order: OrderView }  (404 if not owned)
  POST   /api/orders/:id/cancel -> { order: OrderView }. SERVER-ENFORCED: 409 'Order cannot be cancelled' if status != 'paid'; 403 'Cancellation window expired' if Date.now() > stored cancellable_until (compared against the STORED timestamp, never a client value); on success sets status 'cancelled', restores each order_item's stock, refunds points_redeemed and reverses points_earned.
  POST   /api/orders/:id/buy-again -> CartView (404 if not owned). Re-adds the order's books to the current cart, clamped to current stock; skips out-of-stock/removed books.
  OrderView shape: { id, user_id, status ('pending'|'paid'|'cancelled'), payment_method, subtotal_cents, points_redeemed, points_earned, total_cents, placed_at, cancellable_until, address (parsed JSON snapshot of the chosen address), items: OrderItemRow[], isCancellable:boolean }  (NOTE: raw address_snapshot is NOT exposed; use `address`. isCancellable = status=='paid' && now < cancellable_until.)
  OrderItemRow: { id, order_id, book_id, title, author, unit_price_cents, quantity }
TIMESTAMP NOTE: placed_at/cancellable_until are written as ISO-8601 UTC strings (toISOString). parseSqlTime() in orders.ts also tolerates bare 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' as UTC for any CURRENT_TIMESTAMP rows.
ERROR SHAPE: all errors are JSON { error: string }; VALIDATION -> 400 { error: 'Invalid request body' }; missing/invalid JWT -> 401 { error: 'Unauthorized' } (from authGuard).
Mounted in src/api/index.ts via .use(cartRoutes()).use(addressRoutes()).use(orderRoutes()). Each module is a factory taking an injectable db (defaults to the shared singleton) so tests pass a temp ':memory:' DB (see src/api/commerce.test.ts).
